narratives.Description: bug(ingest): the derived acceptance rung turns every prose sentence of an issue into a clause, even when the body has an explicit Acceptance Criteria list
narratives.Overview:
1. List route. A new function `admittedSourceUnitsFromBody(text)` runs the same quarantine scan as today, then removes fenced code blocks with the existing `stripFencedCodeBlocks`, before anything else. When the result has an Acceptance Criteria heading that `findAcHeading` matches and at least one list item in the section that `sliceAcSection` returns, the units are those list items in order. Each unit is the item line without its bullet and checkbox marker, plus each following line that is indented under it and is not itself a list item, heading or blank line, joined with single spaces. Repeated units are kept once. A checkbox list outside that section and a `Requirements:` list do not select this route.
2. Sentence route. When item 1 finds no list, the units are the sentences of the same scanned, fence-free text as `extractStatementSentences` finds them, except: a heading line ends a span and is never part of a sentence; a line that starts with `Refs`, `Tracking`, `Closes`, `Fixes` or `Part of` followed by an issue number is dropped; a line that starts with the generated-with footer marker is dropped; a blockquote line is dropped; a leading checkbox marker is stripped from a list-item sentence. Inline code is kept as text and never becomes a command.
3. What ingest writes on the body route. On first stamp ingest writes `acceptance.sentences`, `admitted_source_sentences` and `admitted_source_digest` from the item 1 or item 2 units, plus `admitted_source_extractor: 2`. On the list route the plan item titles are the units, so there is one plan item and one clause per criterion. On the sentence route the plan items are found as today, and each plan item title that is not already a unit is added to the sentence list, so every item still has its clause. The issue title is not on the sentence list on either route. `applySentenceListClauses` then writes one clause per sentence-list entry, as today. Captured literal commands are still never copied into `verify_commands`.
4. Version on the pin. A restamp keeps `admitted_source_extractor` with the pin and digest it was written with. In `verify:ac`, both the working-pin live compare and the missing-pin recovery extract the live body with the version stored on the brief: `2` uses `admittedSourceUnitsFromBody`; no field uses `extractAdmittedSourceSentencesFromText` exactly as it is at the dispatch SHA. `extractStatementSentences` and `extractAdmittedSourceSentencesFromText` are not changed; item 2 is a separate function. Outside activation, a git pin keeps today's no-live-compare rule; at activation item 7 applies.
5. Report line. Ingest prints `acceptance: <N> clause(s), <M> plan item(s)` after the created path. It never refuses.
6. Criteria-only record. When the issue has no completed-arc record, ingest looks for a comment that carries an operative `design-critique: not warranted, because ...` line, a `Target-digest:` line and an `## Acceptance Criteria` list, written by the issue's author (the same login as the issue's `user.login`) or by an account whose `repos/<owner>/<repo>/collaborators/<login>/permission` permission or role is `admin`, `maintain` or `write` (the same rule as `hasWritePermission` in `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/forge-approval.ts`). It uses the latest such comment. A permission read that fails leaves that comment unused, as for a commenter without write access. The Target-digest is checked against the live body with the existing `evaluateTargetDigestAdmission`, with the existing stale-target result. The items are the list items of that section, read with the item 1 unit rule (fence-free, wrapped lines joined), and ingest writes them through the existing Spec-path route (`applyHarvestedItemClauses`): one plan item, clause, sentence and pin entry per item. The Spec-path source record names that comment id in `leanCommentId`, its `hashHarvestIdentity` digest in `harvestDigest`, and `kind: "criteria-only"`; a record without `kind` reads as today's lean record. For a brief not on the merge base, `verify:ac` resolves a `criteria-only` record by fetching that comment id from the issue thread, checking it still has the recorded harvest digest and that its author is the issue's author or still has write access by the same lookup, and reading its items with the same rule; a lean record is resolved through the completed-arc record as today. A completed-arc record, when present, is used instead of any criteria-only record. The design-critique ingest posture of such an issue stays `skipped-recorded`.
7. Admitted-source check at activation. When a brief enters `xbrief/active/` (`scope:activate`) and on the pull request that adds it, the existing `verify:ac` admitted-source identity check (#5055) and sentence floor (#3550) run on that brief. For a body-route brief that is not on the merge base, the pin is always compared with the live issue body re-read by the extractor version stored on the pin, even when the pin is loaded from `HEAD` (a `head`-sourced git pin is treated as a working pin for this compare). A pin loaded from the merge base keeps today's no-live-compare rule. A Spec-path pin is compared with its source record as today. Only those two checks run; the clause oracle walk does not. A failure prints the same `verify:ac` message as at completion. No new cause, refusal text or policy flag is added; an existing check runs earlier (operator addition, 2026-11-18).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an issue body with `## Acceptance Criteria` and three list items, plus Summary, Evidence and `Refs #N` prose and the generated footer, when `issue:ingest` runs, then the brief has three plan items, three clauses, a three-entry sentence list and a three-entry pin, all with the item texts, and `admitted_source_extractor: 2`.
- Given a fenced example containing an `## Acceptance Criteria` heading and a bullet, followed outside the fence by the real `## Acceptance Criteria` list, then the plan items, clauses, sentence list and pin hold only the real criteria.
- Given an Acceptance Criteria list item whose text wraps onto an indented second line, then its unit, plan item title and clause hold both lines.
- Given a body with a checkbox under an Evidence heading and plain bullets under `## Acceptance Criteria`, then the units are the Acceptance Criteria bullets only.
- Given a body with checkboxes and no Acceptance Criteria heading, then the sentence route runs and every checkbox item still has a clause.
- Given a body with no list, then no unit starts with a heading word glued onto the next sentence, and no unit is a `Refs`/`Tracking`/`Closes`/`Fixes`/`Part of` line, the footer line or a blockquote line.
- Given a brief ingested under item 3 and an unchanged issue body, when `verify:ac` runs with a working pin and when it runs after the pin was deleted with the digest kept, then neither reports a digest mismatch, an unmapped sentence or a removed identity.
- Given a brief ingested before this change, with no `admitted_source_extractor`, then `verify:ac` gives the same result as at the dispatch SHA in the working-pin compare and in missing-pin recovery.
- Given a restamp of a brief with `admitted_source_extractor: 2`, then the field, pin and digest are unchanged.
- Given any ingest, then the output prints the clause and plan item counts, and the counts never cause a refusal.
- Given an issue with no completed-arc record and a criteria-only record by the issue's author whose Target-digest matches the body and whose list has two items, when `issue:ingest` runs, then the brief has two plan items, two clauses, a two-entry sentence list and pin, and a Spec-path source record with `kind: "criteria-only"` and that comment id.
- Given that brief before it is on the merge base and an unchanged record comment, when `verify:ac` runs, then it reports no digest mismatch, unmapped sentence or removed identity.
- Given a not-warranted comment with an Acceptance Criteria list written by a login that is not the issue's author and has no write access, then ingest does not use it and takes the body route.
- Given a criteria-only record written by an account with write access that is not the issue's author, then ingest uses it as for the issue's author.
- Given an issue with both a completed-arc record and a criteria-only record, then ingest harvests the completed arc's lean.
- Given an ingested brief from which clauses were deleted and whose `admitted_source_digest` was recomputed by hand, when it is activated or its activation pull request is checked, then the activation fails with the `verify:ac` admitted-source digest or identity message, as `scope:complete` would.
- Given a new body-route brief whose clauses, sentence list and pin were shortened and whose digest was recomputed, committed on the branch before the activation pull request is checked, then the activation check compares the `HEAD` pin with the live issue body and fails with the existing admitted-source digest mismatch message.
- Given a body-route brief whose pin is on the merge base, when it is activated, then no live compare runs, as today.
- Given an unchanged ingested brief, when it is activated, then the activation-time check passes.

## In plain English
When an issue states no acceptance command, ingest makes every sentence of the issue body an acceptance clause: the title, headings glued onto the next sentence, evidence, `Refs` lines and the generated footer. It does this even when the body has a clear `## Acceptance Criteria` list. At completion each clause becomes a plan item, so a story with 5 real criteria ends with 29 items, 24 of them noise, and no sanctioned verb removes them. Hand-trimming the brief breaks the admitted-source pin, because `verify:ac` re-reads the same sentences from the live issue body. The recommended fix changes the one function that picks the admitted text from a body: when the body has an explicit list, the list items are the admitted text; when it has none, sentences are picked as today minus headings, reference lines, the footer and quotes. Ingest and `verify:ac` both call that function, and each pin records which version of it made the pin, so stories already in flight keep passing.

The issue has no `## Acceptance Criteria` heading. The three pains below are derived from its `## Expected` section, one per bullet.

## Pains
- P1 — When the issue body has an explicit acceptance list, ingest still makes every prose sentence of the body a clause beside the list items, and `scope:complete` prep turns each clause into a plan item (#6599: 29 items, 24 noise; #6647: 23 clauses, each criterion twice, heading text glued on).
- P2 — When the body has no explicit list, the derived rung still admits text that is not a criterion: a heading glued onto the next sentence, `Refs`/`Tracking` lines, the generated footer and quoted evidence.
- P3 — Ingest does not print the clause count beside the item count, so a mismatch is found only at completion.

## Constraints (not pains)
- No new gate, refusal, grant template or policy flag. A report line is allowed.
- Ingest, the #5055 admitted-source pin and live compare, and the #3550 sentence floor are one surface: the pin, the sentence list and the clauses must come from one selector, and `verify:ac` must re-read the live body with that same selector.
- A brief already ingested (on the merge base or only in a working tree) must give the same `verify:ac` result as before. No remint, no re-ingest, no hand-trim (#6601).
- Do not contradict the accepted arcs on #6644 (synthesis 6969950740: `not_applicable` / `waived` grant values and `scope:confess`) and #6643 (synthesis 6984931843). Those stay the route for noise on briefs already ingested; they are not redesigned here.
- The Spec-path harvest of an accepted arc (#6333 item 2) is unchanged.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- F1. One selector (P1). A new function `admittedSourceUnitsFromBody(text)` replaces `extractAdmittedSourceSentencesFromText` at every call site. After the same quarantine scan, when `extractPlanItems` finds items in the body, the units are those item titles, in order and normalised. Otherwise the units are the sentences, as in F2. On the body route ingest writes the plan item titles, `acceptance.sentences`, the pin and its digest from those units, so the clauses (one per sentence-list entry, as today) equal the items. The issue title is not on the sentence list on this route, as on the Spec-path route.

The sentence picker used by F1 drops: a heading line (it ends a span and is never glued onto the next sentence), a line that starts with `Refs`, `Tracking`, `Closes`, `Fixes` or `Part of` followed by an issue number, a line that starts with the generated-with footer marker, and blockquote lines. - F4. Report line (P3). Ingest prints `acceptance: <N> clause(s), <M> plan item(s)` after the created path. It is a report only.

## In plain English

Ingest currently turns background explanation into acceptance obligations, even when the author supplies a clear acceptance list. A shared selector and a clause-count report address that problem. The recommended mechanism cannot bind as written: any checkbox can suppress real requirements, and the existing list parser drops wrapped portions of criteria.

Answers to Stop 1:

- Given a not-warranted comment with an Acceptance Criteria list written by a login that is not the issue's author and has no write access, then ingest does not use it and takes the body route.
- Given a criteria-only record written by an account with write access that is not the issue's author, then ingest uses it as for the issue's author.

## Summary

When an issue states no literal acceptance command, ingest uses the "derived" rung and turns every prose sentence of the body into an acceptance clause. That includes section headings, evidence, rationale, and the `Refs` and footer lines. It does this even when the body has an explicit `## Acceptance Criteria` checkbox list. `scope:complete` prep (`persistClauseKeyedPendingItems`, `transition.ts:908`) then turns each derived clause into a pending plan item, and no sanctioned verb removes them. The story can only complete through blanket merge evidence or human dispositions on clauses that were never criteria.

## Case

#6599. The body had a 5-item `## Acceptance Criteria` checkbox list plus normal prose: summary, evidence, proposed change, out of scope, and the arc-not-warranted line.
- Ingest produced the 5 correct items. The acceptance block, however, had `source_rung: derived`, `none_stated: true` and 24 more clauses, one per prose sentence, such as "Summary A root-mismatch ...", "Acceptance 1." and "Refs #6594 🤖 Generated with ...".
- At completion the brief had 29 plan items. Finalize refused for lack of evidence on all 29.
- The workaround is `scope:complete --merge-commit <sha> --pr <n>`, which stamps merge evidence on every non-strict item, the 24 noise items included. That makes the acceptance record meaningless for those items.

## Expected

The author should not need to know a special body shape:
- When the body has an explicit acceptance list (`## Acceptance Criteria` checkboxes), that list is the clause source. Derived sentence-harvest is not used, or is limited to the list.
- The derived rung should skip text that is not a criterion: headings, the `Refs`/`Tracking` lines, the generated footer, quoted evidence and code spans.
- Ingest should report the clause count beside the item count, so a mismatch shows before promote or activate. This is a report line, not a new gate.

## Not in scope

No new refusal. Fix what the harvest produces.
